findings.title: The introduction uses unexplained technical language
findings.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
findings.why: Several words are unfamiliar and make the service sound complicated or rather grand, when the three simple steps beneath it make it sound easy.

findings.title: The main illustration has no accessible description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
findings.why: I cannot tell from the supplied description what the picture represents, and a meaningful description would help me understand the example.

findings.title: The primary action does not say what happens next
findings.evidence: [5] link “Proceed →”
findings.why: “Proceed” could mean logging in, starting a story, or something else, although the page context makes the destination reasonably likely.

findings.title: Login fields have no visible labels
findings.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email"; [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
findings.why: Placeholders disappear while I type, so I would like clear labels that stay visible and tell me exactly what each box needs.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: The visible footer links “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” are shown in very faint grey.
findings.why: I may need to read the privacy or terms information, and faint text is difficult for me to see.

findings.title: Unexplained technical error creates doubt after login
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I do not know what “profile sync” means, whether my account is incomplete, or whether continuing could cause a problem.

findings.title: The account greeting uses “Demo” rather than the account holder’s name
findings.evidence: “Welcome back, Demo”
findings.why: It feels impersonal and makes me wonder whether I have reached the correct account.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The footer links “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact,” and the copyright line, appear extremely pale against the background.
findings.why: I can barely read the privacy and contact information, which matters because I want to know how my family details are handled.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy  Terms  Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” are shown in extremely faint grey.
findings.why: I can barely read the privacy and terms links, which are particularly important when entering family information.

findings.title: The essential story fields are not marked required or optional
findings.evidence: The page presents “Where does the story happen?”, “A special object”, and “Tell us the memory or idea behind your story” without saying whether any can be left blank.
findings.why: I want to know whether I must provide every detail before I can continue, particularly because I prefer to complete forms carefully.

findings.title: Footer text has very faint contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy”, “Terms”, “Contact” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear in extremely pale grey against the white footer.
findings.why: I may have difficulty reading these links, and the privacy and terms links are useful when deciding how comfortable I am sharing family information.

findings.title: Footer text is very small
findings.evidence: The Privacy, Terms and Contact links look smaller than the main form text.
findings.why: Small print is difficult for me to read, and these are policy links rather than decorative text.

findings.title: Reading-level choices use unexplained terminology
findings.evidence: The choices are labelled “Lexile BR–200L,” “Lexile 200L–500L,” “Lexile 500L–800L,” and “Lexile 800L+,” with no explanation.
findings.why: I want the book to suit Oliver's age, but these labels do not tell me which option is best for a five-year-old who is learning to read.

findings.title: No selected-age guidance
findings.evidence: Oliver's age was entered previously as 5, but this screen only presents Lexile ranges.
findings.why: I should not have to remember or work out the relationship between age five and these unfamiliar ranges.

findings.title: No confirmation that the complete long memory was saved
findings.evidence: The previous result says the story box “now only shows 200 characters; the end of what you typed was cut off” and ended at “with G”.
findings.why: I am especially concerned that the request that Oliver fly the kite with me may have been lost, which would make the resulting book feel wrong and personal only in part.

findings.title: The photo upload has no visible label
findings.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label); the control displays only “Choose file” and “No file chosen.”
findings.why: I can guess what it is for from the surrounding text, but an explicit label would make the control easier and safer to understand, especially if I were using assistive technology.

findings.title: The privacy handling of a child's photo is not explained before upload
findings.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.” There is no nearby explanation of storage, retention, deletion, sharing, or whether the uploaded photo itself is kept.
findings.why: A photograph of a five-year-old is personal information, and I would not upload one unless I understood why it was needed and what would happen to it.

findings.title: Loading state has no explanatory status text
findings.evidence: The page shows only a circular spinner in an otherwise empty panel.
findings.why: I cannot tell whether my family story is being created successfully, and I may assume I have done something wrong.

findings.title: No way to leave or cancel while waiting
findings.evidence: Only the StoryHearth, How it works, Pricing, My books, and Log out links are visible; the waiting panel has no Cancel or Back control.
findings.why: If the process hangs, I feel trapped and unsure whether I should keep waiting or start again.

findings.title: Generation progress is not explained
findings.evidence: No text explains whether the site is writing the story, preparing illustrations, or saving the book.
findings.why: The lack of context makes the wait feel longer and gives me no reassurance that the story is being personalised from my memory.

findings.title: Spelling error in the book title
findings.evidence: “The Magical Adventrue of Oliver”
findings.why: This is supposed to be a treasured family keepsake, so a visible spelling mistake makes the book look careless and undermines my confidence in the finished product.

findings.title: The cover does not clearly represent the requested family story
findings.evidence: The cover shows Oliver, a house, a sun, and a kite, but no visible Grandma Maggie or identifiable Welsh hill/farmhouse setting.
findings.why: I asked for Oliver to be the hero flying the blue kite with Grandma Maggie on the same hill, and I would like the cover to feel personal rather than generic.

findings.title: Regeneration price is visible without an explanation
findings.evidence: “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
findings.why: I am careful about unexpected costs, and I cannot tell whether this replaces the book, creates an additional version, or makes any changes to an order.

findings.title: Preview controls are not described
findings.evidence: The only visible controls are “‹”, “1 / 9”, and “›”.
findings.why: I can guess what the arrows mean, but written labels would make the reading process more reassuring and accessible.

findings.title: The final story sentence is incomplete
findings.evidence: “And from that day on, whenever Oliver looked up at the sky, he would always remember”
findings.why: It reads as though something has been left out, which makes the finished keepsake feel careless and not properly edited.

findings.title: The final illustration omits the story's central keepsake and relationship
findings.evidence: The final picture shows Oliver and a farmhouse, but no blue kite and no Grandma Maggie.
findings.why: A keepsake should bring together the people and objects that make this family memory special.

findings.title: Gift wrap is selected without my consent
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox “Premium gift wrap” (checked) with “£7.99”
findings.why: I did not ask for gift wrap, and the unexplained extra charge changes the total from £37.98 to £45.97.

findings.title: Optional add-on is not clearly separated from the required cost
findings.evidence: The page shows “Premium gift wrap” and “£7.99” between the hardcover and shipping rows, while the total is “£45.97”.
findings.why: I need to know exactly what is included in the price before deciding whether the book is worth the money.

findings.title: Checkout requests payment and personal details before showing any further useful order information
findings.evidence: The page immediately shows empty “Address” and payment fields, including “Card number”, “Expiry”, and “CVC”.
findings.why: I am cautious about sharing personal and financial information unless I understand exactly why it is needed and can inspect the order safely.

findings.title: The reserved-price countdown may be unnecessary pressure
findings.evidence: [5] “Your price is reserved for 09:57”
findings.why: A countdown can make me feel that I must hurry before understanding the purchase or correcting the gift-wrap selection.
